rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet judged Khadija’s two pre-Islamic children to be in the Fire, then said believers and their children are in Paradise and polytheists and their children in the Fire, citing 52:21.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن عثمان، عن زاذان عن علي، رضي الله عنه، قال: سألت خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report about Khadija’s children singular and weakly grounded because Muhammad ibn Uthman is unknown and Zadhan did not meet Ali.
rows.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب؛ فإن محمد بن عثمان هذا مجهول الحال، وشيخه زاذان لم يدرك عليا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abu Dawud says the female killer and the girl killed are in the Fire; al-Shaʿbi identifies its route through ʿAlqama, Abu Waʾil, and Ibn Masʿud.
rows.anchor: قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الوائدة والموءودة في النار". ثم قال الشعبي: حدثني به علقمة

rows.speaker: سلمة بن قيس الأشجعي
rows.claim: Salama and his brother ask about their mother and an infant sister she buried; the Prophet says both killer and killed are in the Fire unless the mother accepted Islam, and Ibn Kathir grades this chain hasan.
rows.anchor: عن سلمة بن قيس الأشجعي قال: أتيت أنا وأخي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third position suspends judgment about polytheists’ children, relying on the Prophetic answer that God knows what they would have done.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث: التوقف فيهم، واعتمدوا على قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a Bukhari and Muslim report, the Prophet answers Ibn Abbas’s question about polytheist children that God knows what they would have done.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أولاد المشركين قال (6) : الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A second Bukhari and Muslim report gives the same answer when the Prophet is asked about children of polytheists.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه سئل عن أطفال المشركين، فقال: "الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars place polytheists’ children among the people of al-Aʿraf; Ibn Kathir says this returns to the Paradise view because al-Aʿraf is not a permanent abode and its people ultimately enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعلهم من أهل الأعراف. وهذا القول يرجع إلى قول من ذهب إلى أنهم من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement concerns only polytheists’ children; scholars agree Muslim children are people of Paradise, as Qadi Abu Yaʿla reports from Ahmad, and Ibn Kathir says this is the well-known view he affirms.
rows.anchor: فأما ولدان المؤمنين فلا خلاف بين العلماء كما حكاه القاضي أبو يعلى بن الفراء الحنبلي، عن الإمام أحمد

rows.speaker: حماد بن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr reports that Hammad ibn Zayd, Hammad ibn Salama, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and others suspended judgment about all children, resembling Malik’s Muwatta arrangement and hadiths.
rows.anchor: ذهب إلى هذا القول جماعة من أهل الفقه والحديث منهم: حماد بن زيد، وحماد بن سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later Maliki scholars distinguished Muslim children, whom they place in Paradise, from polytheist children left to God’s will; Ibn Kathir calls this very strange and says Malik stated no explicit position.
rows.anchor: وليس عن مالك فيه شيء منصوص، إلا أن المتأخرين من أصحابه ذهبوا إلى أن أطفال المسلمين

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: At an Ansari child’s funeral, ʿAisha calls the child a bird of Paradise, but the Prophet replies that God created both Paradise and Fire with their inhabitants already in their fathers’ loins; Ibn Kathir lists collections transmitting it.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين قالت: دعي النبي (3) صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى جنازة صبي من الأنصار، فقلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Abbas, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya disliked discussing the issue because it needs sound evidence and uninformed claims about revelation are improper.
rows.anchor: كره جماعة من العلماء الكلام فيها، روي ذلك عن ابن عباس، والقاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report Ibn Hibban includes from Ibn Abbas says the community’s affairs remain sound so long as people do not debate children and predestination.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس وهو على المنبر يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يزال أمر هذه الأمة مواتيا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القرطبي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that al-Qurtubi’s al-Tadhkira also gives an account similar to Ibn Abd al-Barr’s discussion.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر أبو عبد الله القرطبي في كتاب "التذكرة" (2) نحو ذلك أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن حبان
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban explains that the debated “children” in the report are children of polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حبان: يعني أطفال المشركين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits the report through Jarir ibn Hazim and notes that others also transmit it from Abu Raja as a statement of Ibn Abbas, not raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقد رواه جماعة عن أبي رجاء، عن ابن عباس موقوفا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The common reading of amarnā is lightened; one interpretation takes it as a decree that leads the affluent to sin, analogous to God’s decree reaching a town, while affirming that God does not command indecency.
rows.anchor: فالمشهور قراءة التخفيف، واختلف المفسرون في معناها، فقيل: معناها أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits from Ibn Abbas, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr also says, that God commanded the affluent to obey but they instead sinned and deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: رواه ابن جريج (6) عن ابن عباس، وقاله سعيد بن جبير أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir allows a reading meaning God made the affluent rulers, which Ibn Kathir says fits the intensive reading ammarna.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: وقد يحتمل أن يكون معناه جعلناهم أمراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ali ibn Talha reports Ibn Abbas’s explanation that God empowered a town’s wicked people, who disobeyed and were destroyed, linking the verse to 6:123; Abu al-ʿAliya, Mujahid, and al-Rabiʿ agree.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها} يقول: سلطنا أشرارها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the phrase means God increased their number; ʿIkrima, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Qatada, and al-Zuhri from Malik give the same explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: {وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها} يقول: أكثرنا عددهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Suwayd ibn Hubayra praises plentiful livestock offspring and a row of pollinated palms; Abu ʿUbayd explains مأمورة as prolific and السكة المأبورة as pollinated palms.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خير مال امرئ له مهرة مأمورة أو سكة مأبورة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd glosses مأمورة as having many offspring, السكة as a straight row of palms, and المأبورة as pollinated; another view treats the expression as paired wordplay like مأزورات غير مأجورات.
rows.anchor: المأمورة: كثيرة النسل. والسكة: الطريقة المصطفة من النخل، والمأبورة: من التأبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns Quraysh that He destroyed nations who denied messengers after Noah; the deniers are no more honored than those peoples and are even more liable to punishment for rejecting the noblest messenger.
rows.anchor: منذرا كفار قريش في تكذيبهم رسوله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه قد أهلك أمما من المكذبين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ten generations lived between Adam and Noah, all adhering to Islam; Ibn Kathir says this is implied by the verse.
rows.anchor: كما قاله (5) ابن عباس: كان بين آدم ونوح عشرة (6) قرون كلهم على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knows and sees every servant’s deed, good or evil, and nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: هو عالم بجميع أعمالهم، خيرها وشرها، لا يخفى عليه منها خافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not everyone who seeks worldly pleasure receives it; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, qualifying other verses that state the promise more generally.
rows.anchor: ما كل من طلب الدنيا وما فيها من النعيم يحصل له، بل إنما يحصل لمن أراد الله ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly seeker who is assigned Hell enters it engulfed on every side, blamed for choosing the fleeting over the lasting and cast away in humiliation.
rows.anchor: إذ اختار الفاني على الباقي {مدحورا}

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿAisha calls this world the home of one without a home and the wealth of one without wealth, gathered by one lacking reason.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الدنيا دار من لا دار له، ومال من لا مال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking its abode and delights by the proper path, namely following the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي: طلب ذلك من طريقه وهو متابعة الرسول {وهو مؤمن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker must believe in the heart, affirming reward and requital; then the person’s effort is accepted and appreciated.
rows.anchor: أي: وقلبه مؤمن، أي: مصدق بالثواب والجزاء {فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies both worldly and afterlife seekers from His gift; as sovereign judge He gives each what is decreed and none can block or alter His decision.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من الفريقين الذين أرادوا الدنيا والذين أرادوا الآخرة، نمدهم فيما هم فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets God’s unrestricted gift as not diminished; al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd interpret it as not withheld.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: {وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا} أي: منقوصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly people differ in wealth, appearance, and lifespan, but differences among people in the afterlife are greater, from Hell’s depths to Paradise’s highest ranks.
rows.anchor: فمنهم الغني والفقير وبين ذلك، والحسن والقبيح وبين ذلك، ومن يموت صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in both the depths of Hell and the ranks of Paradise differ among themselves; Paradise has one hundred levels, each separated by the distance between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: فإن الجنة مائة درجة ما بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says inhabitants of the highest ranks see the people of ʿIlliyyin like a distant star on the horizon.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين: "إن أهل الدرجات العلى ليرون أهل عليين، كما ترون الكوكب الغابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses accountable members of the community: worship God without a partner, or you will be blamed and abandoned because God will leave you to a powerless false deity; only God controls harm and benefit.
rows.anchor: والمراد المكلفون من الأمة، لا تجعل أيها المكلف في عبادتك ربك له شريكا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that taking one’s distress to people does not relieve it, while entrusting it to God brings near or prompt sufficiency; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أصابته فاقة فأنزلها بالناس لم تسد فاقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here qaḍā means command: God commands worship of Him alone and kindness to parents, as in the command to thank God and one’s parents in 31:14.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى آمرا بعبادته وحده لا شريك له؛ فإن القضاء هاهنا بمعنى الأمر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains qaḍā as enjoined; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Ibn Masʿud, and al-Dahhak are reported to read the phrase with waṣṣā, “enjoined.”
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: {وقضى} يعني: وصى، وكذا قرأ أبي بن كعب، وعبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the smallest expression of irritation is forbidden; parents must not hear bad speech or receive ugly conduct.
rows.anchor: لا تسمعهما قولا سيئا، حتى ولا التأفيف الذي هو أدنى مراتب القول السيئ

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah explains “do not rebuke them” as not shaking a hand at one’s parents.
rows.anchor: كما قال عطاء بن أبي رباح في قوله: {ولا تنهرهما} أي: لا تنفض (6) يدك على والديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding bad speech and conduct, God commands kind, gentle, pleasant speech delivered with courtesy, reverence, and respect.
rows.anchor: أمره بالقول الحسن والفعل الحسن فقال: {وقل لهما قولا كريما} أي: لينا طيبا حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing of humility means behaving humbly toward parents and praying for mercy for them in old age and at death, as they raised the child when small.
rows.anchor: {واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة} أي: تواضع لهما بفعلك {وقل رب ارحمهما} أي: في كبرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 9:113 was later revealed, forbidding the Prophet and believers to seek forgiveness for polytheist relatives.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم أنزل الله [تعالى] (1) : {ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Anas and others lists three disgraces, including a person who reaches aged parents yet is not brought into Paradise; Ibn Kathir says Gabriel prompted the Prophet’s three amens.
rows.anchor: رغم أنف امرئ أدرك أبويه أو أحدهما فلم يدخلاه الجنة، قل: آمين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports from Malik ibn al-Harith and Malik ibn ʿAmr al-Qushayri promise Paradise to one who cares for a Muslim orphan and describe freeing a Muslim slave as ransom from the Fire; they also warn against neglecting aged parents.
rows.anchor: من ضم يتيما بين أبوين مسلمين إلى طعامه وشرابه حتى يستغني عنه، وجبت له الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Malik al-Qushayri reports that a person who reaches one or both parents and then enters Hell is distanced and crushed away; al-Tayalisi also transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن مالك القشيري قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أدرك والديه أو أحدهما ثم دخل النار

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet condemns the person who reaches one or both parents in old age and still fails to enter Paradise; Ibn Kathir calls this route sound and notes Muslim alone transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رغم أنف، ثم رغم أنف، ثم رغم أنف رجل أدرك والديه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra combines failure to bless the Prophet, failure to gain Ramadan’s forgiveness, and failure to enter Paradise through aged parents; al-Tirmidhi calls this route gharib.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رغم أنف رجل ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي

rows.speaker: أبو أسيد مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي
rows.claim: Asked how to honor deceased parents, the Prophet lists praying for them, seeking forgiveness, carrying out their bequest, honoring their friends, and maintaining kinship through them; Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أسيد وهو مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي، قال: بينما أنا جالس عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Jaahima, who seeks advice about campaigning, to stay with his mother because Paradise is at her feet; al-Nasaʾi and Ibn Majah transmit the report.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية بن جاهمة السلمي؛ أن جاهمة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet repeats that God recommends fathers once, mothers three times, and then the closest relatives; Ibn Majah also transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن المقدام بن معد يكرب (1) الكندي، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله يوصيكم بآبائكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man from Banu Yarbuʿ hears the Prophet rank the giver’s mother and father, then sister and brother, followed by the next nearest relatives.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من بني يربوع قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسمعته وهو يكلم الناس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man carrying his mother during circumambulation asks whether he fulfilled her right; the answer is not even for one groan, and al-Bazzar says this report is known only by this route.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان بن بريدة، عن أبيه؛ أن رجلا كان في الطواف حاملا أمه يطوف بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the report about carrying one’s mother during circumambulation weak because al-Hasan ibn Abi Jaʿfar is weak.
rows.anchor: قلت: والحسن بن أبي جعفر ضعيف، والله أعلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the verse covers a child’s impulsive act toward parents when the child’s heart and intention are good and no harm is meant.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرجل تكون (9) منه البادرة إلى أبويه، وفي نيته وقلبه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the repentant or returning people as obedient worshippers who pray.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: للمطيعين أهل الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the term as those who glorify God, with another report from him glossing it as obedient benefactors.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: المسبحين. وفي رواية عنه: المطيعين المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters say the term refers to those who pray between the evening prayers or perform the forenoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هم الذين يصلون بين العشاءين. وقال بعضهم: هم الذين يصلون الضحى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib defines the returning person as one who commits a sin, repents, sins again, and repents again; ʿAta ibn Yasar agrees.
rows.anchor: قال: الذي يصيب الذنب ثم يتوب، ويصيب الذنب ثم يتوب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr explain the term as people who return to what is good.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير: هم الراجعون إلى الخير

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Mujahid transmits from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr that the returning person remembers sins in private and asks God to forgive them; ʿUmayr also describes such a person as vigilant in seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد عن عبيد بن عمير في قوله: {فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا} قال: هو الذي إذا ذكر ذنوبه

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the meaning “repentant from sin,” returning from disobedience to obedience and from what God dislikes to what He loves; Ibn Kathir says this is correct because the word derives from returning.
rows.anchor: والأولى في ذلك قول من قال: هو التائب من الذنب، الراجع عن المعصية إلى الطاعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report says the Prophet, when returning from a journey, would say that they were returning, repenting, worshipping, and praising their Lord.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا رجع من سفر قال (5) : آيبون تائبون عابدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After parental kindness, the passage turns to kindness toward relatives and maintaining kinship ties, echoing reports that rank the mother, father, and nearest relatives first.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى بر الوالدين، عطف بذكر الإحسان إلى القرابة وصلة الأرحام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises expanded provision and a longer life to whoever wishes to maintain kinship ties.
rows.anchor: من أحب أن يبسط له رزقه (1) وينسأ له في أجله، فليصل رحمه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Abu Saʿid that, when this verse came down, the Prophet called Fatima and gave her Fadak; Ibn Kathir finds the chronology problematic because the verse is Meccan and Fadak was conquered in year seven.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال لما نزلت، هذه الآية {وآت ذا القربى حقه} دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Fadak report would be difficult to reconcile if its chain were sound, since Fadak was conquered with Khaybar in 7 AH while the verse is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث مشكل لو صح إسناده؛ لأن الآية مكية، وفدك إنما فتحت مع خيبر سنة سبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier discussion in Surat al-Tawba already covered the poor and the wayfarer, so Ibn Kathir does not repeat it here.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على المساكين وابن السبيل في "سورة براءة" بما أغنى عن إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending is commanded, but extravagance is forbidden; spending should be moderate, as described in 25:67.
rows.anchor: لما أمر بالإنفاق نهى عن الإسراف فيه، بل يكون وسطا، كما قال في الآية الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasteful spenders resemble devils in extravagance, foolishness, abandoning obedience, and committing disobedience; Satan is ungrateful because he denies God’s blessing and disobeys Him.
rows.anchor: أي: في التبذير والسفه وترك طاعة الله وارتكاب معصيته؛ ولهذا قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When relatives and other people owed support ask while the giver has no money, the giver should turn them away gently and promise help when provision arrives.
rows.anchor: وإذا سألك أقاربك ومن أمرنا بإعطائهم وليس عندك شيء، وأعرضت عنهم لفقد النفقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others interpret the kind, easy speech as a gentle promise of future assistance.
rows.anchor: هكذا فسر قوله {فقل لهم قولا ميسورا} بالوعد: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition shows God is more merciful to servants than a parent to a child; pre-Islamic Arabs sometimes killed daughters to reduce household costs and did not inherit them.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية الكريمة دالة على أن الله تعالى أرحم بعباده من الوالد بولده؛ لأنه ينهى [تعالى] (12) عن قتل الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse forbids killing children for fear of future poverty and puts their provision before the parents’; 6:151 instead addresses existing poverty and puts the parents’ provision first.
rows.anchor: أي: خوف أن تفتقروا في ثاني الحال؛ ولهذا قدم الاهتمام برزقهم فقال: {نحن نرزقهم وإياكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that killing children is a grave sin; some readers pronounce the word خطأ, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: أي: ذنبا عظيما. وقرأ بعضهم: "كان خطأ كبيرا" وهو بمعناه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In a sound report, Ibn Masʿud asks the Prophet for the gravest sins: associating a partner with God, killing one’s child for fear of sharing food, then adultery with a neighbor’s wife.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن عبد الله بن مسعود: قلت: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers both fornication and approaching its causes; it is a grave indecency and a wicked path.
rows.anchor: ناهيا عباده عن الزنا وعن مقاربته، وهو مخالطة أسبابه (6) ودواعيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a young man asks permission to fornicate, the Prophet asks whether he would accept it for female relatives; the man says no, and the Prophet prays that God forgive, purify, and protect him, after which he no longer turns toward it.
rows.anchor: إن فتى شابا أتى النبي (7) صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، ائذن لي بالزنا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya says that after associating partners with God, no sin is greater than a man placing semen in a womb forbidden to him.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من ذنب بعد الشرك أعظم عند الله من نطفة وضعها رجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The sound collections say Muslim blood is lawful only in three cases: life for life, a married adulterer, and one who abandons religion and the community.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in the Sunan says the destruction of the world is less serious before God than killing a Muslim.
rows.anchor: وفي السنن: "لزوال الدنيا أهون عند الله من قتل مسلم (3) "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The murdered person’s heir has legal authority over the killer and may exact retaliation, accept blood money, or pardon without payment, as established by the Sunna.
rows.anchor: سلطة على القاتل، فإنه بالخيار فيه إن شاء قتله قودا، وإن شاء عفا عنه على الدية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas inferred that Muawiya would rule because he was guardian of murdered Uthman; Muawiya demanded Uthman’s killers from Ali, refused allegiance until then, and eventually gained power as Ibn Abbas predicted.
rows.anchor: وقد أخذ الإمام الحبر ابن عباس من عموم هذه الآية الكريمة ولاية معاوية السلطنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Zuhdam al-Jarmi recounts Ibn Abbas advising Ali to withdraw and predicting Muawiya’s rule; he also foretells Persian and Roman customs and non-Muslim rule, urging adherence to known guidance.
rows.anchor: عن زهدم الجرمي قال: كنا في سمر ابن عباس فقال: إني محدثكم حديثا ليس بسر ولا علانية

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Interpreters explain “do not exceed in killing” as forbidding the heir to mutilate the killer or to exact retaliation against anyone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: قالوا: معناه: فلا يسرف الولي في قتل القاتل بأن يمثل به أو يقتص من غير القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heir is supported against the killer by law and, in the ordinary course of events, by divine decree.
rows.anchor: أي أن الولي منصور على القاتل شرعا، وغالبا قدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan’s property may be managed only for the orphan’s benefit; Ibn Kathir links this to 4:2 and 4:6, and cites the Prophet warning Abu Dharr not to govern two people or manage an orphan’s wealth.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تتصرفوا له إلا بالغبطة {ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم إنه كان حوبا كبيرا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill covenants and contracts made with people, since those who make them will be questioned about them.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تعاهدون عليه الناس والعقود التي تعاملونهم بها، فإن العهد والعقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measure fully without shortchanging or diminishing people’s goods.
rows.anchor: وقوله [تعالى] (4) : {وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم} أي: من غير تطفيف، ولا تبخسوا الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qistas is read with either a damma or kasra on qaf, is like qirtas, and means a balance; Mujahid says it means justice in Roman speech.
rows.anchor: قرئ بضم القاف وكسرها، كالقرطاس وهو الميزان. وقال مجاهد: هو العدل بالرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A straight balance has no crookedness, deviation, or instability; fair dealing benefits worldly life and the afterlife and yields the best final outcome.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {المستقيم} أي: الذي لا اعوجاج فيه ولا انحراف ولا اضطراب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Saʿid transmits Qatada’s gloss that the instruction gives the best reward and outcome.
rows.anchor: قال: سعيد، عن قتادة: {ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا} أي: خير ثوابا وعاقبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas warns that faulty measuring and weighing destroyed earlier peoples; a report from the Prophet says God replaces unlawful gain abandoned from fear of Him with something better, first in this life.
rows.anchor: وأما ابن عباس كان يقول: يا معشر الموالي، إنكم وليتم أمرين بهما هلك الناس قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All those” refers to hearing, sight, and the heart; a person will be questioned at the Resurrection about them and how they were used.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {كل أولئك} أي: هذه الصفات من السمع والبصر والفؤاد {كان عنه مسئولا} أي: سيسأل العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative أولئك can be used where تلك is expected; Ibn Kathir cites an unnamed poet’s line as evidence.
rows.anchor: ويصح استعمال "أولئك" مكان "تلك"، كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse forbids arrogance and strutting like tyrants; walking proudly cannot cut through the earth or reach the mountains.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى ناهيا عباده، عن التجبر والتبختر في المشية: {ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا} أي: متبخترا متمايلا

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir explains “you will not pierce the earth” as being unable to cut through it and cites a line by Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjaj as lexical evidence.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن جرير، واستشهد عليه بقول رؤبة بن العجاج: وقاتم الأعماق خاوي المخترق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report tells of a man strutting in two cloaks who was swallowed by the earth and continues sinking in it until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيح: "بينما رجل يمشي فيمن كان قبلكم، وعليه بردان يتبختر فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun likewise came out in finery and was swallowed by the earth; another report says God raises the humble and lowers the arrogant in people’s esteem.
rows.anchor: وكذلك (4) أخبر الله [تعالى] (5) عن قارون أنه خرج على قومه في زينته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan rebukes Ibn al-Ahtam’s proud dress and gait as foolish, ungrateful use of blessings that neglects God’s commands and rights; the man apologizes and Hasan tells him to repent.
rows.anchor: فقال: أف أف، شامخ بأنفه، ثان عطفه، مصعر خده، ينظر في عطفيه

rows.speaker: البختري العابد
rows.claim: Al-Bukhturi the ascetic tells a man of Ali’s family that this proud gait is not the gait of someone God honored; the man stops.
rows.anchor: فقال له: يا هذا، إن الذي أكرمك به لم تكن هذه مشيته! قال: فتركها الرجل بعد

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar tells a swaggering man that devils have brothers who walk like this.
rows.anchor: ورأى ابن عمر رجلا يخطر في مشيته، فقال: إن للشياطين إخوانا

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan warns against swaggering and remarks that a man’s hand is a part of his body.
rows.anchor: وقال: خالد بن معدان: إياكم والخطر، فإن الرجل يده من سائر (11) جسده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that when the community walks in a swaggering manner and Persians and Romans serve them, God will set some people over others.
rows.anchor: عن يحنس قال: قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا مشت أمتي المطيطاء، وخدمتهم فارس والروم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: On the reading سيئة, Ibn Jarir takes all the prohibitions from killing children through this point as culpable sins hated by God.
rows.anchor: أما من قرأ "سيئة" أي: فاحشة. فمعناه عنده: كل هذا الذي نهينا عنه

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: On the construct reading سيئه, Ibn Jarir takes all the material from the command to worship God alone onward as having a bad part hated by God.
rows.anchor: وأما من قرأ {سيئه} على الإضافة فمعناه عنده: كل هذا الذي ذكرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded noble character traits and forbidden vile traits are wisdom revealed to Muhammad so he can command people to follow them.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي أمرناك به من الأخلاق الجميلة، ونهيناك عنه من الصفات الرذيلة، مما أوحينا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating another god brings blame from oneself, God, and people; Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain being cast away as being expelled.
rows.anchor: أي: تلومك نفسك [ويلومك الله] (1) والخلق. {مدحورا} . قال ابن عباس وقتادة: مطرودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although addressed to the Messenger, the warning is meant for the community through him, since the Prophet is protected from sin.
rows.anchor: والمراد من هذا الخطاب الأمة بواسطة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم؛ فإنه صلوات الله وسلامه عليه معصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists make three grave errors: call God’s servant angels female, claim they are God’s daughters, and worship them; the verse challenges why God would choose daughters for Himself while giving them sons.
rows.anchor: فجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا، ثم ادعوا أنهم بنات الله، ثم عبدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs themselves disdained daughters and sometimes killed them, making their claim a grossly unjust division; Ibn Kathir links the rebuttal to 19:88–95 denying that God has a child.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلكم ولده الإناث التي تأنفون (4) أن يكن لكم، وربما قتلتموهن بالوأد، فتلك إذا قسمة ضيزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an varies warnings to make people remember its proofs, signs, and admonitions and turn from shirk, wrongdoing, and falsehood, but its wrongdoers only recoil farther from truth.
rows.anchor: صرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يذكرون ما فيه من الحجج والبينات والمواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If other gods existed as the polytheists claim, they would worship and seek nearness to the Lord of the Throne; people therefore should worship God directly, since intermediaries are neither needed nor approved and all messengers forbade them.
rows.anchor: لكان أولئك المعبودون يعبدونه ويتقربون إليه ويبتغون إليه الوسيلة والقربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted far above the unjust claim that He has other gods and is uniquely One, self-sufficient, without offspring or peer.
rows.anchor: بل هو الله الأحد الصمد، الذي لم يلد ولم يولد، ولم يكن له كفوا أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens, earth, and all creatures glorify, exalt, and declare God’s oneness in lordship and divinity, in contrast to the polytheists’ claims; Ibn Kathir cites 19:90–92 about creation nearly breaking over the claim of a divine child.
rows.anchor: تقدسه السموات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن، أي: من المخلوقات، وتنزهه وتعظمه وتجله

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن قرط
rows.claim: A report about the Night Journey says the Prophet heard the highest heavens glorifying God with praise while returning from Jerusalem; Ibn Kathir gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن قرط؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسري إلى المسجد الأقصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every created thing glorifies God, but people do not understand its praise because it is in a language unlike theirs; the more famous of two views includes animals, plants, and inanimate things.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في الحيوانات (5) والنبات والجماد، وهذا أشهر القولين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says they heard food glorifying while it was being eaten; the report is in Sahih al-Bukhari.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: كنا نسمع تسبيح الطعام وهو يؤكل

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A well-known report says the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman heard pebbles in their hands glorifying like bees humming.
rows.anchor: أن النبي (7) صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ في يده حصيات، فسمع لهن تسبيح كحنين النحل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells people not to overburden mounts or use them as seats for roadside conversations, since some mounts remember God more than their riders.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم: "اركبوها سالمة، ودعوها سالمة، ولا تتخذوها كراسي لأحاديثكم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report in al-Nasaʾi says the Prophet forbade killing frogs because their croaking is glorification.
rows.anchor: وفي سنن النسائي عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل الضفدع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits from ʿAbd Allah ibn Babi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that basic declarations of faith, praise, greatness, glorification, and reliance are forms of creation’s prayer and praise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة، عن عبد الله بن بابي (12) ، عن عبد الله بن عمرو: أن الرجل إذا قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report tells of an Arab criticizing the Prophet for raising a low-status shepherd and lowering a nobleman; the Prophet rebukes his brocade clothing and recounts Noah’s counsel to avoid shirk and pride and to say the two glorifications, which are creation’s prayer and source of provision.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعرابي عليه جبة من طيالسة مكفوفة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits a longer version of Noah’s counsel to his sons about avoiding shirk and pride and saying the testimony of faith and God’s praise; Ibn Kathir says this transmission is unique.
rows.anchor: ورواه الإمام أحمد، أيضا، عن سليمان بن حرب، عن حماد بن زيد، عن الصقعب (5) بن زهير

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Jabir says Noah told his son that glorifying God is creation’s prayer and means of provision; Ibn Jarir links it to this verse but Ibn Kathir notes its chain is weak because Musa ibn ʿUbayda is weak to most critics.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، رضي الله عنه (7) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أخبركم بشيء أمر به نوح ابنه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says columns and trees glorify; some early authorities add that a door’s creaking and flowing water are their glorification.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة في قوله تعالى: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: الأسطوانة تسبح، والشجرة تسبح

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri transmits from Mansur that Ibrahim said food glorifies; Ibn Kathir says the prostration verse at the start of Surat al-Hajj supports this view.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري، عن منصور، عن إبراهيم قال: الطعام يسبح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another view restricts glorification to beings with life: Qatada includes anything with a spirit, such as a tree, and al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the same.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: كل شيء فيه الروح يسبح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In a report about a wooden table, al-Hasan says it used to glorify; Ibn Kathir infers that it did so while alive and green but stopped when cut and dry.
rows.anchor: فقدموا الخوان، فقال يزيد الرقاشي: يا أبا سعيد، يسبح هذا الخوان؟ فقال: كان يسبح مرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says two grave-dwellers were punished for failing to guard against urine and for carrying tales; the Prophet placed moist palm branches on their graves hoping their punishment would lessen until they dried.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ جريدة رطبة، فشقها نصفين، ثم غرز في كل قبر واحدة، ثم قال: "لعله يخفف عنهما ما لم ييبسا"

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars explain the palm branches’ effect as their glorification while green and moist, which ends when they dry; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال بعض من تكلم على هذا الحديث من العلماء: إنما قال: "ما لم ييبسا" لأنهما يسبحان ما دام فيهما خضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing and forgiving: He delays punishment for sinners, but takes those who persist in disbelief and defiance; those who abandon sin and repent receive forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أي: إنه [تعالى] (6) لا يعاجل من عصاه بالعقوبة، بل يؤجله وينظره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says God gives an oppressor respite until He seizes him and does not let him escape; the Prophet then recites 11:102.
rows.anchor: كما جاء في الصحيحين: "إن الله ليملي للظالم، حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته". ثم قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links this ending to 35:41–45: God alone holds the heavens and earth, and delays judgment to a fixed term rather than destroying every creature for its deeds.
rows.anchor: كما قال في آخر فاطر: {إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd identify the hidden barrier as coverings on disbelievers’ hearts, linking it to 41:5, where they say their hearts, ears, and the space between them are veiled from the message.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة، وابن زيد: هو الأكنة على قلوبهم، كما قال تعالى: {وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective مستور can mean covering or protective, like words such as ميمون and مشؤوم.
rows.anchor: أي: بمعنى ساتر، كميمون ومشئوم، بمعنى: يامن وشائم؛ لأنه من يمنهم وشأمهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Another view says the barrier is invisible to sight yet still blocks guidance; Ibn Jarir prefers this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مستورا عن الأبصار فلا تراه، وهو مع ذلك حجاب بينهم وبين الهدى

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asma reports that when Umm Jamil came to Abu Bakr taunting the Prophet after Surat al-Masad was revealed, the Prophet said she would not see him and recited this verse; she stood by Abu Bakr but could not see him.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر [الصديق] (2) رضي الله عنها (3) ، قالت: لما نزلت {تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart-coverings prevent understanding the Qur’an, and the ear’s heaviness prevents hearing it in a way that benefits and guides.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة} : جمع "كنان"، الذي يغشى القلب {أن يفقهوه} أي: لئلا يفهموا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet recites God alone and says “there is no god but God,” the polytheists turn away fleeing; نفورا can be a plural noun or a verbal noun, and 39:45 describes their aversion.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده} أي: إذا وحدت الله في تلاوتك، وقلت: "لا إله إلا الله"

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the polytheists rejected the Muslims’ declaration of God’s oneness, which weighed on them and Satan’s forces; God nevertheless makes the declaration prevail and grants victory through it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله: {وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا} إن المسلمين لما قالوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An unusual report from Ibn Abbas interprets those who turn away as devils; Ibn Kathir rejects this as a very strange interpretation, while noting devils do withdraw at Qur’an, the call to prayer, and remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا} هم الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh leaders secretly listened to the Prophet reciting and called him enchanted, either by sorcery or, as some lexically suggested, a human nourished by food; Ibn Jarir approved the latter sense, which Ibn Kathir questions because they meant a possessed man.
rows.anchor: بما قالوا من أنه رجل مسحور، من السحر على المشهور، أو من "السحر"، وهو الرئة، أي: إن تتبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word مسحر meaning fed or human is witnessed by a line attributed to an unnamed poet and a rajaz line; Ibn Jarir favors this lexical explanation, but Ibn Kathir doubts it here.
rows.anchor: فإن تسألينا فيم نحن فإننا … عصافير من هذا الأنام المسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers also called Muhammad a poet, soothsayer, madman, or sorcerer; these comparisons led them astray, leaving them no path to truth or escape from error.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال: "شاعر"، ومنهم من قال: "كاهن"، ومنهم من قال: "مجنون"، ومنهم من قال: "ساحر"

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from al-Zuhri that Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, and al-Akhnas secretly listened to the Prophet at night for three consecutive nights, each unaware of the others, then pledged not to return.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق في السيرة: حدثني محمد بن مسلم (10) بن شهاب الزهري،

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
rows.claim: Al-Akhnas asks Abu Sufyan what he heard from Muhammad; Abu Sufyan says he understood some of it but not the meaning or intent of other parts, and al-Akhnas agrees.
rows.anchor: والله لقد سمعت أشياء أعرفها وأعرف ما يراد بها، وسمعت أشياء ما عرفت معناها، ولا ما يراد بها

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl explains he will never believe Muhammad because Banu Abd Manaf had matched his clan in generosity and prestige, then claimed prophethood and revelation, a status Abu Jahl says his group could never attain.
rows.anchor: تنازعنا نحن وبنو عبد مناف الشرف: أطعموا فأطعمنا، وحملوا فحملنا، وأعطوا فأعطينا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses رفات as dust or soil, while Ali ibn Abi Talha transmits Ibn Abbas’s gloss as dust; the disbelievers deny being raised anew after decay.
rows.anchor: أي: ترابا. قاله مجاهد. وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: غبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial concerns being raised on Judgment Day as a new creation after becoming nothing; Ibn Kathir links this to 79:10–12 and 36:78–79.
rows.anchor: أي: يوم القيامة {خلقا جديدا} أي: بعد ما بلينا وصرنا عدما لا يذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones and iron are harder to restore than bones and dust, so the challenge means that resurrection is possible even if people became more resistant forms.
rows.anchor: وهما (2) أشد امتناعا من العظام والرفات {أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Asked about whatever seems greatest in people’s hearts, Ibn Abbas says through Mujahid that it is death; Ibn Umar says even if people became dead, God would revive them, as do Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: سألت ابن عباس عن ذلك فقال: هو الموت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives heaven, earth, and mountains as other possible forms, and another report from him says to become whatever one wishes because God will restore people after death.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم} يعني: السماء والأرض والجبال

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: In Malik’s transmitted commentary from al-Zuhri, the phrase is explained as the Prophet; Malik also says people explain it as death.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري في قوله {أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم} قال: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir cites the report that death itself will be brought on Judgment Day as a white ram, recognized by the people of Paradise and Hell and slaughtered so both know they will never die; no grading is given here.
rows.anchor: حديث: "يجاء بالموت يوم القيامة كأنه كبش أملح، فيوقف بين الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who first created people can restore them in any form, as also stated in 30:27.
rows.anchor: أي: الذي خلقكم ولم تكونوا شيئا مذكورا، ثم صرتم بشرا تنتشرون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain the head-shaking as a mocking gesture; Ibn Kathir says the word means moving from bottom to top or top to bottom, like an ostrich chick bobbing its head.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: يحركونها استهزاء. وهذا الذي قالاه هو الذي تفهمه العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نغض is also used of a tooth moving and rising from its socket; a rajaz poet illustrates it with a line about teeth loosened by old age.
rows.anchor: ويقال: نغضت (11) سنه إذا تحركت وارتفعت من منبتها؛ قال: الراجز (12)
